items.name: Abdulrazak Gurnah
lines: In Paradise, Gurnah recast the story of Joseph around Yusuf’s journey in colonial East Africa. Readers familiar with the earlier story encounter a young man facing a very different choice at the end.

By the Sea brings Saleh Omar and Latif Mahmud together in England after their families’ histories have crossed in Zanzibar. Gurnah lets each man’s account alter what the reader understands about the other.
In Admiring Silence, Gurnah’s narrator invents a past for the English family he lives among. Readers have to follow both what he chooses to tell them and what maintaining that story costs him.
In Afterlives, Gurnah follows people caught up in German colonial rule in East Africa. The aftereffects of military service unfold through the lives of families as well as soldiers.

items.name: Tarja Halonen
lines: In February 2002 Tarja Halonen accepted the ILO Director-General's invitation to co-chair the World Commission on the Social Dimension of Globalization alongside Tanzania's President Benjamin Mkapa, taking on a body created to produce an authoritative report on how the global economy affects work.

As co-chair with Namibia's Sam Nujoma, Finland's President Tarja Halonen called the United Nations Millennium Summit to order on 6 September 2000 in New York, opening the heads-of-state gathering with a declaration and a minute of silent prayer or meditation.

While a Finnish parliamentarian at the Council of Europe's Parliamentary Assembly, Tarja Halonen proposed creating a monitoring committee for member states' commitments; the assembly adopted it as Order 488 (1993), which became known as the Halonen Order.

In her speech opening Parliament's 2009 session, President Tarja Halonen told legislators that the Mine Ban Treaty and the Convention on Cluster Munitions had forced development of new weapons systems, often clearly more expensive even if more effective than existing ones.

items.name: Gordon Parks
lines: For American Gothic, Washington, D.C., Parks photographed government cleaner Ella Watson with a mop and broom in front of an American flag. The tools of her job and the national emblem occupy the same frame.
For Harlem Gang Leader, Parks followed teenager Red Jackson and his circle. Moving between street encounters and quieter moments gave the picture story more than one way to see its subject.
In Segregation Story, Parks photographed Black families going about daily life in Alabama. Color, clothing and a sign above a doorway can show how segregation shaped an ordinary outing.

Parks worked with Ralph Ellison to make photographs in conversation with Invisible Man. A man emerging from a street opening translates a literary image of invisibility into something the camera can show.

In 2007, Novak and Jelena Djokovic founded an organization focused on early childhood education. Its work in Serbia includes developing preschools and supporting the people who teach in them.

items.name: Altiero Spinelli
lines: While held by the Fascist regime on the island of Ventotene, Spinelli worked with Ernesto Rossi and Eugenio Colorni to draft a federalist manifesto, completed in June 1941, calling for a free and united Europe; the text later circulated within the Italian Resistance.

Spinelli circulated a letter to fellow MEPs asking colleagues who agreed that institutional reform was too important to leave to statesmen and diplomats to reply and meet to plan how Parliament could take part; eight answered, gathering in July 1980.

Altiero Spinelli, as European Commission member with responsibility for industrial, technological and scientific affairs, delivered a speech on the current state of industrial policy to the Council of Ministers of Foreign Affairs in Luxembourg on 25 June 1974.

As rapporteur-coordinator of Parliament's institutional committee, Spinelli steered the drafting of a treaty text; on 14 February 1984 the European Parliament adopted the Draft Treaty Establishing the European Union by an overwhelming majority.

In January 1997, after Democrat Xavier Becerra became chair of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus following a trip to Cuba, Ros-Lehtinen and Lincoln Diaz-Balart resigned from the caucus, protesting that Havana meeting.
In 2011 she became the first Republican cosponsor of the Respect for Marriage Act, Jerrold Nadler's bill to repeal the Defense of Marriage Act.

During the global HIV/AIDS crisis, Representative Ileana Ros-Lehtinen worked on the federal government's PEPFAR program, the President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief, and later called PEPFAR one of her proudest achievements as a Member of Congress.

As justice minister, Campbell reintroduced firearms legislation as Bill C-17, which received royal assent on December 5, 1991, after the Montreal massacre; it followed Bill C-80, which had stalled at second reading amid opposition from rural and western backbenchers.
As defence minister, Campbell told the Commons on May 11, 1993, that she had instituted a board of inquiry into the conduct of Canadian forces in Somalia.

Campbell chaired the independent advisory board that was asked to recommend qualified, functionally bilingual Supreme Court candidates in 2016 and 2017, under a process the government set and whose shortlists the minister of justice reviewed.

items.name: Berthe Morisot
lines: In The Cradle, a woman watches a sleeping infant through a veil of white fabric. The bend of her arm echoes the baby’s arm, connecting them across the space between their faces.
Summer’s Day seats two women in an open boat. Morisot lets brisk marks for light and water remain visible around them, so the still figures share the movement of the lake.
In The Harbor at Lorient, Morisot puts her sister on a low wall and the working harbor across the water. It is possible to follow the sitter’s downward gaze and still take in the far shore.
Hanging the Laundry out to Dry sets people doing the wash within a broad, open landscape. The line of pale fabric gives the eye a way across the canvas and gives everyday work a place in the view.

items.name: Guillermo del Toro
lines: In The Devil’s Backbone, a boy enters an orphanage during the Spanish Civil War and encounters a ghost. Del Toro lets the boy’s attempts to understand a haunting lead him into the history of the place.

In Pan’s Labyrinth, Ofelia’s stepfather issues military orders while a faun sets her a series of tasks. Hearing instructions from both figures turns the question of whom to obey into a choice the child must make.

In The Shape of Water, a cleaner who cannot speak meets an amphibious captive in the laboratory where she works. Their exchanges through gesture and touch give viewers a courtship they can follow without spoken conversation.

For Pinocchio, del Toro and his collaborators used physical puppets and sets. MoMA exhibited motion tests and working sets that let visitors see how tiny changes of pose became a performance on screen.

items.name: Martin Luther King Jr.
lines: During the Montgomery bus boycott, King led the Montgomery Improvement Association as residents sustained the protest for more than a year. He helped turn individual refusals to ride into a shared demand for change.

Writing from a Birmingham jail in 1963, King answered clergy who had criticized the demonstrations. He explained why a request to wait for a better time carried a different cost for the people denied their rights.

At the March on Washington in August 1963, King moved between an account of unfulfilled American promises and a vision of what equality could mean for children. The crowd could picture the future the marchers were asking for.

In Beyond Vietnam, delivered at Riverside Church in 1967, King publicly explained why he opposed the war. He connected the resources devoted to fighting abroad with the needs of poor communities at home.

In Beijing in 2015, Felix won the world 400-metre title. Her earlier global titles had come over 200 metres, and this time she had to sustain her race for a full lap.

items.name: Kim Young-sam
lines: In 1993 the Kim Young-sam administration instituted the Real Name Financial Transactions System through the Presidential Emergency Order for National Finance and Economy, banning anonymous financial accounts and requiring accounts to be held under real names.

Korea acceded to the OECD in December 1996, which the OECD report describes as the culmination of two decades of nation building by the Korean people and government, in a document whose presidential chronology lists Kim Young-sam as holding office from 1993 to 1998.

During the presidential election the Real Name Deposit system became a salient political issue, and President Kim Young-sam later implemented it in 1993 through the Presidential Financial and Economic Emergency Decree on Real Name Financial Transaction and Guarantee of Secrecy, aimed at the underground economy, with preparations kept confidential until his announcement.
Kim Young-sam became South Korea's first civilian president, elected in 1993, following the restoration of direct presidential elections in 1987.

On January 11, 2022, in the Schladming night slalom, she recorded her 47th career World Cup slalom victory, surpassing Ingemar Stenmark's record for wins in a single discipline.

items.name: Mary Anning
lines: After her brother Joseph found an ichthyosaur skull near Lyme Regis, Anning excavated the rest of the skeleton. The assembled animal gave researchers more to compare than an isolated fossil bone.
In 1823 Anning unearthed a nearly complete plesiosaur. Its unusually long neck could be studied from an articulated skeleton instead of reconstructed from scattered fragments.
Anning also recovered a pterosaur from the cliffs at Lyme Regis. It supplied evidence of a winged reptile in Britain, far from the German localities then known for such finds.
Anning drew attention to the fish remains inside objects found among marine reptile fossils. Her observations helped William Buckland identify some of the objects as fossilized droppings.

items.name: Sri Mulyani Indrawati
lines: In a World Bank Live discussion on finance for an equitable recovery, Finance Minister Sri Mulyani Indrawati described Indonesia's pandemic budget approach, saying the government focused fiscal spending on health, social safety nets and small and medium enterprises while deepening tax reform.

At the April 2024 Development Committee meeting, Sri Mulyani Indrawati, speaking for a constituency of eleven countries, welcomed the World Bank Group Evolution Roadmap and argued that a capital increase tied to a shareholding review would strengthen the bank's legitimacy and governance.

Welcoming a World Bank development policy loan, Finance Minister Sri Mulyani Indrawati said that since 2019 the Indonesian government had focused on tax and expenditure reforms, and that the support would strengthen fiscal sustainability and spur broad-based growth after the pandemic.

As World Bank Managing Director and Chief Operating Officer from 2010, Sri Mulyani Indrawati oversaw operations worldwide, shaped strategy for the Fund for the Poorest, IDA, and chaired the Bank's Advisory Council on Gender and Development.

Campaigning for the February 1997 election, Bhutto alleged irregularities in the voting but stopped short of calling for mass protests, saying Pakistan needed above all political stability to improve the domestic situation.

In 1948, the Founding Junta of the Second Republic was established by a solemn oath to restore constitutional life, and José Figueres Ferrer was named its president.

items.name: Fanny Blankers-Koen
lines: At the 1948 London Olympics, Olympic rules limited athletes to three individual events plus a relay, so Blankers-Koen entered the 100m, 200m and 80m hurdles and the 4x100m relay, opting not to contest the high jump or long jump even though she was the world-record holder in both. She ran 11 races in eight days in London and won them all.

After winning four events in London in 1948, Blankers-Koen rode through Amsterdam in a public parade. When asked about the excitement surrounding her, she described the achievement simply as winning some footraces.

Before the 1952 Helsinki Olympics she ran her fastest-ever times for 100 yards, 100m and 200m, but, suffering from a painful carbuncle on her leg, she withdrew from the 100m semi-finals to save her strength for the 80m hurdles final, then pulled up in that final after hitting the first two hurdles hard. She was still top of the world lists for the 80m hurdles in 1953 with 11.1.

From a 1936 Olympic debut in which she finished fifth in the high jump and 4x100m relay, she went on to serve as Dutch athletics team manager from the 1958 European Championships to the Mexico City 1968 Olympic Games, and the Netherlands' prominent FBK Games in Hengelo, an annual fixture since 1981, is named after her and held in a stadium that also bears her name.

On April 11, 2024, Foreign Secretary Alicia Bárcena announced at the National Palace that Mexico had filed suit against Ecuador before the International Court of Justice over the raid on its Quito embassy, arguing Ecuador must answer for violating the embassy's inviolability and attacking diplomatic personnel.

On 20 May 2019, Bárcena presented to President López Obrador in Mexico City ECLAC's proposal for a Comprehensive Development Plan for El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras and Mexico, which called for orderly migration flows from Central America and for greater public and private investment.

items.name: Elinor Ostrom
lines: For her dissertation, Ostrom studied how water users around Los Angeles organized to manage a groundwater basin. She followed the local institutions people actually built to address a shared shortage.

In studies of American metropolitan policing, Ostrom and her colleagues compared which services small and large departments could deliver. They examined individual tasks before judging the size of a whole organization.

In Nepal, Ostrom’s team compared irrigation systems managed by farmers with systems managed by government agencies. Their comparison gave farmers’ working rules a place alongside the physical condition of the canals.

In experiments on shared resources, Ostrom and her collaborators let some participants talk face to face. They could then compare what people actually took when conversation was possible with what happened when it was barred.

lines: Eugenia Charles, Dominica's prime minister and chairman of the Organization of Eastern Caribbean States, joined Ronald Reagan at the White House on 25 October 1983, where Reagan announced that the United States had received a formal request from the five OECS member nations to help restore order and democracy in Grenada.

During Dominica's 1979 political crisis, opposition leader Eugenia Charles served on the Committee for National Salvation, which brokered an interim government to administer the country until general elections could be organized.
After a December 1981 coup attempt in Dominica, Prime Minister Mary Eugenia Charles imposed a state of emergency while police searched mountain forests for men who had fled after the failed coup.

In March 1994, Britain's Foreign Office told Parliament that Charles had discussed the EC banana regime with ministers and, on a Saturday in Dominica, gave them a document on restructuring the Windward Islands banana industry, which was then under study.

items.name: Katsushika Hokusai
lines: In Under the Wave off Kanagawa, three boats pitch beneath a breaking wave while Mount Fuji sits small in the distance. The curl of the water frames the very mountain the wave seems large enough to swallow.
South Wind, Clear Sky gives Mount Fuji nearly the entire sheet. The broad red slope and narrow streaks of cloud make the same landmark recognizable with very little detail.
In The Amida Falls, water pours from a round opening while three figures picnic on a ledge. Their stillness gives the eye somewhere to pause beside the rushing waterfall.
In The Ghost of Kohada Koheiji, a skeletal figure peers over the rim of a mosquito net. A familiar household object becomes the thin boundary between a sleeping person and the ghost.

items.name: Helmut Kohl
lines: Chancellor Helmut Kohl surprised the Bundestag on 28 November 1989 by presenting a multi-step plan for unification with a democratizing East Germany: closer cooperation between the two states, then confederation, then federation, compatible with détente and European integration.

At a 22 September 1984 ceremony at Verdun marking the seventieth anniversary of the First World War's outbreak, Kohl stood hand in hand with French President François Mitterrand at the Douaumont Ossuary before memorial wreaths, an image widely read as Franco-German reconciliation.

On 13 December 1991 Kohl told the Bundestag that the European Council had agreed at Maastricht, after more than thirty hours of talks, on treaties for political union and economic and monetary union, calling the path to European union irreversible.

During a July 1990 working visit to the Soviet Union, Kohl met Mikhail Gorbachev to discuss the terms of German reunification; in return for considerable payments and economic support, Gorbachev raised no objections to a united Germany belonging to NATO.

lines: Midway through the 1988 season, in his first year as Alain Prost's McLaren teammate, Senna was asked at a press conference whether it was possible for the two to be equal; he answered that there could only be one winner, a reply Formula 1's retrospective records.

After taking pole for the 1988 Monaco Grand Prix, Senna kept going faster and ended the session over two seconds quicker than Prost in an identical McLaren, then told Formula 1's Hall of Fame profile that the lap frightened him and that he drove back to the pits slowly and did not go out again that day.

During his 1984 rookie season with Toleman, Senna opened talks with Lotus in the background, which Formula 1's profile describes as a breach of his Toleman contract, and he was suspended for a race late that year.
At the 1985 Portuguese Grand Prix, Senna took the first pole position and first win of his Formula 1 career, race day run in wet conditions, as Formula 1's profile records.

items.name: Mary Shelley
lines: In Frankenstein, Shelley lets an Arctic explorer relay Victor Frankenstein’s story and Victor relay the creature’s. Each speaker asks someone else to hear a version of events that might otherwise be lost.

For History of a Six Weeks’ Tour, Mary and Percy Shelley brought travel journals and letters into a shared account of a European journey. Domestic details and political observations sit alongside descriptions of the landscape.
The Last Man gives a future plague a witness who lives long enough to remember the people it has taken. Shelley approaches a catastrophe on a world scale through the narrowing circle of one narrator.
For the 1831 edition of Frankenstein, Shelley wrote an introduction describing how the story began. Readers received a separate account of the novel’s creation in its author’s own voice.

items.name: Mark Rutte
lines: At the UN General Assembly's 69th session general debate, Dutch Prime Minister Mark Rutte said the 298 passengers of flight MH17 would be alive without the Crimea conflict and eastern Ukraine's destabilization, noting 196 victims were Dutch nationals.

In a speech on 19 December 2022, Prime Minister Mark Rutte apologised for the Dutch State's past actions to enslaved people worldwide and their descendants. He delivered the apology at the National Archives in The Hague before representatives of organisations that had pressed for acknowledgement of slavery's effects.

In 2020, Dutch Prime Minister Mark Rutte co-wrote op-eds with the leaders of Austria, Denmark and Sweden opposing a large EU recovery fund and grants-based pandemic assistance, as the so-called Frugal Four resisted increasing the multiannual budget.

On taking office as NATO Secretary General, Mark Rutte named stepping up support for Ukraine and bringing it closer to NATO as his second priority, saying Europe cannot have lasting security without a strong, independent Ukraine.

In her 29 November 2023 remarks to Pacific Emerging Leaders, Wong recounted that Tuvalu asked Australia to enhance the partnership through climate adaptation, security and mobility with dignity, presenting the Falepili Union as Australia's answer to that request.

The Australia-Tuvalu Falepili Union text, tabled in Parliament, records the parties committing to enhance their partnership on prosperity, stability and security including by responding to climate change as a shared security concern.

At the Tuvalu State Dinner in Funafuti, Wong described welcoming Tuvalu's request to elevate the relationship and said she was proud to agree shared understandings with Prime Minister Feleti on bringing the Falepili Union to life through close community consultation.

items.name: Kader Asmal
lines: In the April 1997 foreword to the White Paper on a National Water Policy, Asmal called for national water policy and the water law to be reviewed so that water would be shared equitably. The document's context section stated that South Africa's water law had applied the rules of the well-watered colonising countries of Europe to an arid and variable climate.
Asmal chaired the World Commission on Dams, which reported in December 2000 after an independent global review of the costs and benefits of large dam projects.

At the London launch of the commission's final report on 16 November 2000, the speaker recalled that Asmal, as Minister of Water Affairs, had faced the hard choice of relocating some so that all might have water, or forgoing a dam.
Asmal was chairperson of the Irish Anti-Apartheid Movement from 1972 until 1991, organising opposition to apartheid from his base in Dublin.

items.name: Simón Bolívar
lines: On 6 September 1815, while in Kingston, Jamaica, Simón Bolívar wrote a letter addressed to a British subject, later identified as Henry Cullen of Falmouth, setting out his arguments for Latin American independence and seeking British support.

On 15 February 1819, Simón Bolívar delivered a speech at the Second Constituent Congress of Venezuela in Angostura, addressing the congressmen on the constitutional project and Venezuela's situation, a text he had drafted in late 1818 and shown to Manuel Palacio Fajardo for comment.

As head of state of Peru, Simón Bolívar issued a convocation on 7 December 1824 in Lima, two days before the Battle of Ayacucho, inviting the governments of Gran Colombia, Mexico, Río de la Plata, Chile and Central America to install an assembly of plenipotentiaries in Panama.

On 15 June 1813 in Trujillo, Simón Bolívar issued the Decreto de Guerra a Muerte, a proclamation declaring war to the death against royalist forces in Venezuela following the fall of the First Republic.

items.name: Mario Draghi
lines: Addressing an investment conference in London on 26 July 2012, ECB President Mario Draghi said the central bank was ready, within its mandate, to do whatever it takes to preserve the euro, citing convertibility risk premia as falling within the ECB's remit.

At a Nicosia press conference on 5 March 2015, Mario Draghi said the ECB would begin buying euro-denominated public sector securities in the secondary market on 9 March. Combined public and private purchases were set at €60 billion a month.

Speaking in Strasbourg on 17 September 2024, Mario Draghi said he had presented his report on the future of Europe's competitiveness to the European Commission President the previous week, opening a Parliament presentation of the report.

On 27 April 2021 Mario Draghi, as prime minister, addressed the Senate with government communications ahead of transmitting Italy's National Recovery and Resilience Plan to the European Commission, placing the plan before parliament before its submission.

On 14 February 2006 Vice President Lu convened female officials and elected representatives at a tea party, proposing a nationwide association for female political figures to work with her Democratic Pacific Union.
Speaking at the Harvard ITASA conference in 2002, Vice President Lu suggested that China and Taiwan each first adopt one system, namely freedom and democracy, instead of 'one country, two systems.'

items.name: Mary Robinson
lines: Mary Robinson, as President of Ireland, became the first Head of State to visit Rwanda soon after the 1994 genocide. At the conference she framed the discussion around Rwanda's post-genocide problems and the role of women in reconstruction and peace restoration.

Speaking at the UN Commission on the Status of Women on 8 March 1994, Robinson said she had come directly from Somalia to speak for the people she met there who could not speak for themselves, and urged the empowerment of women.

In a February 1995 address to both Houses of the Oireachtas, Robinson recalled committing her presidency to the seventy million people worldwide claiming Irish descent and argued Irishness should be broad and inclusive rather than territorial.

Mary Robinson served as the UN Secretary-General's Special Envoy on Climate Change in the run-up to the Paris Agreement, a post she held until the end of December 2015, when the COP21 summit concluded with the historic climate accord.

items.name: Frederick Douglass
lines: In his 1845 Narrative, Douglass recounted learning to read while enslaved and the efforts made to prevent it. A personal history placed before readers became an argument about who controlled access to knowledge.
In Rochester, Douglass founded The North Star, an antislavery newspaper. Editing it gave him a way to address readers regularly and publish voices alongside his own.

Invited to speak about Independence Day in 1852, Douglass asked what the celebration meant to people still enslaved. He made the distance between his listeners’ freedom and others’ captivity the subject of the speech.
During the Civil War, Douglass helped recruit Black soldiers and met Abraham Lincoln to raise the treatment they faced. He carried grievances about pay and protection directly to the president.

At the apology ceremony in Nuuk on 24 September 2025, Frederiksen addressed Greenlandic women and girls who had been fitted with contraceptive devices, many against their will. Speaking for Denmark, she apologised directly to those affected.

Addressing Ukraine's Verkhovna Rada on 6 September 2023, Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said Danish F-16 aircraft were urgently wanted in Ukraine, praised Ukrainian pilots' eagerness to bring them home, and welcomed Ukraine's movement closer to the European Union and NATO.

In her address to the UN General Assembly, Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said Denmark was committed to vaccine solidarity and COVAX and would scale up Danish grant-based climate finance to at least $500 million a year by 2023.

items.name: Gabriel García Márquez
lines: In One Hundred Years of Solitude, García Márquez followed generations of the Buendía family in Macondo. Marvels enter the town’s history in the same matter-of-fact voice as ordinary family events.

The Autumn of the Patriarch returns repeatedly to the death of a dictator. The shifting accounts make it difficult for the reader to separate one man’s life from the stories that maintained his power.
For The Story of a Shipwrecked Sailor, García Márquez reconstructed a Colombian sailor’s days adrift through interviews. He told the account in the survivor’s voice.

García Márquez opened his Nobel lecture with the traveler Antonio Pigafetta’s extraordinary accounts of South America. He then asked European listeners to consider the limits of their own ways of interpreting Latin America.

items.name: Eva Perón
lines: In a national radio address on women’s suffrage, Eva Perón argued that Argentine women already shared the obligations of civic life and should have a vote in its decisions. She took that case directly to women listening around the country.

In 1948, the María Eva Duarte de Perón Social Aid Foundation was created; its Hogar de Tránsito Nº 2, the largest, offered women from across the country free lodging, food and assistance, and on leaving they received work tools and other aid.

In 1949, Eva Perón personally selected 23 delegates, one per province or territory and one for the Federal Capital, to conduct a national census of women as the first step in organizing the Peronist women's party.

On 22 August 1951, at the Cabildo Abierto rally organized by the CGT, Eva Perón publicly received the proposal to be vice-presidential candidate and asked for time to respond, before announcing her renunciation by radio five days later.

In his September 20, 1968 House of Commons maiden speech, Lincoln Alexander stated he accepted the responsibility of speaking for all Canadians who feel they are subjects of discrimination because of race, creed or colour.
Lincoln Alexander served as the first Chair of the Canadian Race Relations Foundation, an appointment cited in a 2017 government statement marking Lincoln Alexander Day.

Lincoln Alexander resigned his parliamentary seat to become Chair of the Ontario Workers' Compensation Board in 1980, leading the board for five years until 1985 before his appointment as Ontario's Lieutenant Governor.

lines: On 16 May 2012, Dilma Rousseff opened Brazil's National Truth Commission with a speech in Brasília, arguing that under democracy truth, memory and history should come to the surface and become known, especially for new and future generations.

At the NET Mundial conference in São Paulo, she signed the Marco Civil da Internet and defended freedom of expression and privacy online, saying the interception of communications of citizens, companies, diplomatic representations and the presidency was unacceptable.

At the 68th UN General Assembly in September 2013, Dilma Rousseff condemned a global electronic espionage network, noting that Brazilian diplomatic representations and the presidency itself had their communications intercepted, and defended an internet framework to prevent new abuses.

In her Senate impeachment defense of August 2016, Rousseff argued a political conviction requires a proven crime of responsibility and asked senators to weigh what they felt for the country and people over personal resentments.

lines: Under Michael Manley's premiership, his government introduced the Bauxite Levy in 1974, requiring the production levy to be paid on all bauxite or laterite extracted or won in Jamaica on or after 1 January 1974.
JAMAL and the Basic School Development Programmes were initiatives of Manley's new government, which also introduced free secondary education.
Michael Manley met Fidel Castro in late 1973, after which his government expanded ties with Cuba, part of a broader leftward shift during the 1970s.
Under its Democratic Socialism programme, Manley's government introduced a Minimum Wage Law, compulsory recognition of labour unions, and maternity leave for women.

On 25 July 1821, José de San Martín issued a bando in Lima announcing to Peruvians that the solemn proclamation of independence would take place on Saturday the 28th, and asking the noble vecindario to attend the oath, adorn and illuminate its houses on the nights of Friday, Saturday and Sunday.

As Protector of Peru, José de San Martín issued the so-called "Ley de vientres," a legal norm that had given good results in Buenos Aires and freed from slavery those born from 28 July 1821 onward.

lines: “Water No Get Enemy” builds its argument out of an everyday necessity. Fela lets the band establish the groove before he begins listing the things people need water to do.
In “Zombie,” Fela barks out drill commands and the backing singers answer. The band turns the sound of soldiers obeying orders into a taunt anyone in the crowd can repeat.

On “Expensive Shit,” Fela turns a police attempt to catch him with marijuana into an extended comic story. The punch line depends on listeners following the evidence almost as closely as the police do.
